CODEX_TRANSCRIPT_DIR = attacker-owned 0777 dir -> 'refusing transcript directory', rc=1, nothing written. Symlinked named dir and planted latest.jsonl link: refused (tests). TMPDIR unset -> /tmp/sb-codex-transcripts.XXXXXX 0700. Sweep: victim's own old dir removed but its inner symlinks to ~/important not followed (target intact); attacker-owned old dir, attacker symlink and victim symlink named sb-codex-transcripts.* (aged 3 days) all left alone (-type d, -user, no -L). TMPDIR given as a symlink without trailing slash makes the sweep a no-op (harmless). Residual: see minor 2 (named dir that is the user's own but was world-writable).

issues.problem: The brief scanner still lets real-shaped literal secrets through. (a) scan() never applies the _AUTH_HEADER and _PASSWORD_FLAG patterns that redact() already treats as secrets, so 'Authorization: Basic <base64 user:pass>', 'Authorization: token <40-char token>', 'Proxy-Authorization: Basic ...', '--token <value>' and '--password <value>' (space form) pass the gate. (b) The new UUID exemption applies whatever the name, so UUID-shaped API keys (Heroku API keys are UUIDs) pass: 'HEROKU_API_KEY=3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c2f-1a6b8d0e5f3c', 'client_secret=<uuid>'. (c) The SCREAMING_SNAKE exemption applies to digit-bearing values, so 'TOKEN=AB12_CD34_EF56_GH78_IJ90' and 'API_KEY=XK9A_P2MQ_7VR4_TL8N_B3CW' pass (caught at r1 fbf2842, missed at r2 and r3: same identifier-exemption class as the r2 major). (d) Trivial passwords are exempt on any host: 'https://admin:admin@prod-db.company.com'. (e) Pre-existing gaps: names ending in a generic *_KEY (AZURE_STORAGE_KEY=<88-char base64>, signing_key=<random>) and '-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----' with a body are neither scanned nor redacted.
issues.evidence: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -I REVF-G6b-r3-probe/c3.py and c4.py and corpus2.py against the worktree agent_redact.py: scan() returns None for each string above, while redact() rewrites the Authorization and --token/--password ones to [REDACTED]. Same probe against fbf2842 (r1) catches 'TOKEN=AB12_CD34_EF56_GH78_IJ90' (assignment).
issues.suggested_fix: In scan(), run _AUTH_HEADER (any scheme) and _PASSWORD_FLAG and test the value with _looks_random(..., bearer=True) / _is_reference. Exempt UUIDs only when the assignment name is not a strong secret name (api_key, secret, client_secret, password, private_key) or only for id-like names (csrf/session/request/trace/correlation). Restrict the SCREAMING_SNAKE exemption to digitless segments or segments that read as words (e.g. at most a trailing numeric suffix: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET_2). Limit trivial-password exemption to localhost/127.0.0.1/::1/*.local/docker service names. Add PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK to the PEM pattern and consider [_-]key names with long base64/random values. Pin every sample in tests/python/test_agent_redact.py.

issues.problem: A named CODEX_TRANSCRIPT_DIR that the user owns but that is group/world-writable is accepted and then chmod'ed 700; files already planted in it by another user (regular files, not links) are written into, not replaced. The attacker who planted a 0666 latest.jsonl keeps an fd open and reads the raw, unredacted prompt and transcript (redaction replaces the inode afterwards); the attacker-owned latest.meta.json stays 0666 because chmod 600 fails. A named directory under an attacker-writable non-sticky parent can also be swapped after the check. CODEX_TRANSCRIPT_DIR is set only by live-test isolation, so exposure is low.
issues.evidence: Probe: victim (uid 65534) owns $S/tmp/vnamed 0777; attacker (root) plants latest.jsonl/latest.meta.json 0666 and holds them open; victim runs codex_capture_transcript with CODEX_TRANSCRIPT_DIR=$S/tmp/vnamed -> 'chmod: changing permissions of .../latest.meta.json: Operation not permitted'; the attacker's fd reads '{"type": "prompt.submitted", "prompt": "my private prompt password=hunter2hunter2X9\n"}' and 'Bearer abcdefgh12345678XYZ' (unredacted).
issues.suggested_fix: Refuse a named directory that is group/world-writable (or any existing entry not owned by the user), and create latest.jsonl/meta/archive with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW (write to mkstemp in the dir, then rename).

issues.problem: The trivial-password exemption is not pinned: emptying _TRIVIAL_PASSWORDS leaves the unit tests green (the only honest sample is postgres:postgres, which passes through the user==password rule).
issues.evidence: Sandbox mutation REVF-G6b-r3-probe/mut: `_TRIVIAL_PASSWORDS = set()` -> python3 -m unittest test_agent_redact: OK. Other mutations fail as expected (no Stripe/webhook rules: 2 failures; no UUID exemption: 2; PEM header-only: 2).
issues.suggested_fix: Add an honest sample such as postgres://user:password@localhost/db.

issues.problem: Nits: the new non-blocking drain has no hard-deadline or size check, so a background grandchild that floods stdout from the instant of the drain would keep it reading (the main loop already accumulates unbounded output, so this is the same pre-existing memory class). The 4 MiB fingerprint cap means a change past 4 MiB in a same-size untracked file is invisible to the quota-retry check; not documented next to the other fingerprint residuals. The sweep uses `-mtime +1` (effectively 2 days) while the comment says 'older than a day'.
issues.evidence: Static reading; the 4 MiB case reproduced (fingerprint 2186461316 before and after changing byte 4,500,000 of a 5 MB file).
issues.suggested_fix: Check hard_deadline inside the drain loop; mention the 4 MiB cap in the Quota row; align the sweep comment.
